small_guidance:
- The scatter kernel uses atomic_add per (N, D_in*H_in*W_in, OC tile) — autotune BLOCK_OC over {32, 64} and num_warps over {2, 4}, num_stages=2; also try increasing BLOCK_IC to next_pow2(IC)=32 (already) but split OC into multiple programs to expose more parallelism.
- For the softmax+sigmoid kernel, S = 32*64*64 = 131072 launches per batch — autotune over BLOCK_C ∈ {64} with num_warps ∈ {1,2,4} since C=64 is small; consider tiling S in the program (process multiple spatial points per program) to amortize launch overhead.
- Fold the bias add into the scatter kernel epilogue rather than expanding bias into the output buffer with a clone (saves a full O(N·OC·D_out·H_out·W_out) write before the kernel even starts).
large_guidance:
- Replace the scatter-add ConvTranspose3d with a gather-based GEMM formulation: one program per (N, OC tile, D_out·H_out·W_out tile), where each output position (d_o,h_o,w_o) gathers the contributing (d_i,h_i,w_i,kd,kh,kw) tuples (those satisfying d_o+pad_d-kd ≡ 0 mod stride_d and within bounds). This eliminates atomics entirely and turns the op into a tiled matmul of shape (OC, IC·KD·KH·KW) × (IC·KD·KH·KW, spatial_out_tile), which is the standard high-throughput pattern. SMEM budget on RTX-4090: BLOCK_M=32, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=16, num_stages=2 fits comfortably.
- Fuse the softmax+sigmoid pass directly with the conv-transpose epilogue is not feasible (softmax needs a reduction across OC which a single OC-tiled program doesn't have), so keep them separate, but make the softmax kernel persistent over (N, spatial) with one program per spatial column reading the full C=64 axis into registers — current launch grid of 16·16·32·32·2·2·2 = 524288 programs is the bottleneck after the conv; tile multiple spatial points per program (e.g. 8 spatial × 64 channels) to cut launches 8×.
- Drop the bias-expand-and-clone path; allocate output with torch.empty and have the GEMM kernel initialize its tile with bias broadcast on the first K-iteration (no atomics, no pre-fill).
